title: contains
summary: Test whether text inputs contain patterns in MATLAB and RunMat.

gpu_support.notes: Runs on the CPU. RunMat has no resident text-array representation; resident numeric values reject as nontext before provider access.

description: `contains(str, pattern)` returns logical results indicating whether each element of `str` contains the corresponding text in `pattern`. It supports string arrays, character arrays, and cell text inputs with implicit expansion behavior matching MATLAB and RunMat.
behaviors: Accepts text inputs as string scalars/arrays, character scalars/arrays, or cell arrays of character vectors.
Accepts patterns in the same formats. Either input may be scalar; when sizes differ MATLAB-style implicit expansion applies.
Missing string scalars (`<missing>`) never match any pattern.
Empty pattern values (`""` or `''`) always match non-missing text elements.
The optional `'IgnoreCase', true|false` name-value pair controls case sensitivity (default is case-sensitive).
Returns a logical scalar when the broadcasted size is one element, otherwise returns a logical array with the broadcasted shape.

examples.description: Check if a string contains a substring
Apply a scalar pattern to every element of a string array
Match element-wise patterns with implicit expansion
Search a cell array of character vectors
Provide multiple patterns as a column vector
Handle empty and missing text values

faqs.question: What types can I pass to `contains`?
faqs.answer: Use string scalars/arrays, character vectors/arrays, or cell arrays of character vectors for both the text and the pattern. Mixed combinations are accepted, and RunMat performs MATLAB-style implicit expansion when the array sizes differ.

faqs.question: How do I ignore letter case?
faqs.answer: Specify `'IgnoreCase', true` after the pattern argument. The option name is case-insensitive and the default is `false`. Positional, numeric, and textual flag conveniences are available only in RunMat compatibility mode.

faqs.question: What happens with empty patterns?
faqs.answer: Empty patterns (`""` or `''`) always match non-missing text elements. When the text element is missing (`<missing>`), the result is `false`.

faqs.question: Can I search for multiple patterns at once?
faqs.answer: Yes. Provide `pattern` as a string array, character array, or cell array of character vectors. RunMat applies implicit expansion so that scalar inputs expand across the other argument automatically.

faqs.question: How are missing strings treated?
faqs.answer: Missing string scalars (displayed as `<missing>`) never match any pattern and produce `false` in the result. Use `ismissing` if you need to separate missing values before calling `contains`.

faqs.question: Does `contains` run on the GPU?
faqs.answer: No. The builtin executes on the CPU, and RunMat has no GPU-resident text representation. Numeric gpuArray values reject as nontext before provider access.

faqs.question: Does `contains` preserve the input shape?
faqs.answer: Yes. The output is a logical array whose shape is the implicit-expansion result of the input shapes. When the broadcasted shape has exactly one element, the builtin returns a logical scalar.

gpu_residency: `contains` executes on host text values. RunMat currently has no GPU-resident string representation, so a numeric gpuArray is rejected as nontext before any provider download.
gpu_behavior: `contains` performs host-side text comparisons and registers no provider hook. Resident numeric inputs reject before provider access because they are not text values.
